extracted.intended_audience: senior/key personnel and other significant contributors preparing NIH-style biographical sketches for grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and example content for preparing an NIH-format Biographical Sketch for senior/key personnel and other significant contributors, including required sections, formatting, and example entries (Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, Contributions to Science, Research Support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified section ordering and headings for each person and ensure the complete biosketch does not exceed five pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name, eRA Commons user name, and position title
rubrics_metrics.description: NAME: [Full name]  eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login):  POSITION TITLE:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the individual's full name, their eRA Commons username (or credential), and their current position title at the top of the biosketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training table
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rows with INSTITUTION AND LOCATION, DEGREE (if applicable), Completion Date MM/YYYY, and FIELD OF STUDY. Start with the baccalaureate and include subsequent training (residency, postdoc) as applicable; add or delete rows to fit the individual's history.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a concise personal statement summarizing the applicant's qualifications, relevant experience, current roles, and how their background prepares them to contribute to and/or mentor on the proposed project. Use the personal statement to justify the individual's suitability for their role on the application (examples in the document illustrate mentorship, relevant research focus, collaborative experience, and contributions to the proposed aims).

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List academic and professional positions with dates (chronological), and selected honors. Include position titles, institution names, and date ranges. Honors should be listed (selected) and may include awards, scholarships, committee memberships, and advisory roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numbered thematic descriptions of major scientific contributions (e.g., 1., 2., 3.), each with a short explanatory paragraph describing the contribution's significance, influence (for example on policy or practice), and context. Under each contribution, include representative citations (a., b., c.) with full references and identifiers (PMID/PMCID when available). Use examples to show how to link contributions to impact (policy change, method development, clinical recommendations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative publications and citation detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Within Contributions to Science and elsewhere, include specific publications as evidence (formatted with authors, title, journal, date, volume/pages) and include PubMed IDs/PMCID links when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite key papers supporting each described contribution. Provide sufficient bibliographic detail (authors, journal, year, PMID/PMCID) so reviewers can identify the work. A link to a complete list of published work (e.g., MyBibliography URL) may be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Research Support (ongoing and completed)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. RESEARCH SUPPORT  Ongoing Research Support  Completed Research Support
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List current (ongoing) and past (completed) research support with grant number and PI designation (e.g., 1U50CK000198-01 (Schaffner)), dates (MM/DD/YYYY or MM/YYYY ranges), funding agency, project title, a brief descriptive summary of the project's purpose/aims, and the individual's role (e.g., PI, Co-Investigator, Investigator). Include descriptions that state goals and scope and, where relevant, specify responsibilities or roles on multi-site/umbrella projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent, role-specific descriptions in Research Support entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Research Support entry should state the grant identifier, dates, Agency, Title, Description, and Role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure entries clearly identify whether support is ongoing or completed, the award period, the funding agency, the project title, a short description of aims and scope, and the individual's role on the project to clarify potential overlaps with the proposed work.
